rows.evidence: Q1: Section 3 (Case analysis), Fig. 7, Fig. 9, Tables 3-4 - the authors run their own field validation in a 13 ha jujube orchard in Alar, Xinjiang (2021 harvest), comparing yield under their space-information management scheme versus traditional management, UAV-based yield estimation versus harvest counts, and harvest path economics.
rows.notes: The study does not deploy or evaluate soil moisture sensors, nor does it report any irrigation adjustment or fruit-quality outcome attributable to soil or tree-growth monitoring. Its 'space information' consists of agrometeorological satellite weather data and UAV images (fruit close-ups and orchard panoramas) used for yield estimation and harvest path planning; soil information is only mentioned generically in the method description (Section 2.2) as something technicians could combine, with no measurement. The only quality-related result (average selling price in Table 3) is attributed to harvest timing/path planning, not to irrigation management. Scheme 1 vs 2 yield comparison (Fig. 7) is for the whole 'full-process program' with no soil sensor or irrigation component described. No dispersion statistics, no limitations beyond weather effects on image segmentation (Table 5), which concern yield prediction rather than the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a UAV/satellite-based management, yield-estimation and harvest-path-planning case study on one jujube orchard; it contains no soil sensor data and no irrigation experiment, so it cannot support the cited claim.
